universe_note: Chain-level campaign-v1 screen (identity_schema campaign-v1, scenario_id null). Every row is an exact selection-handoff candidate resolved through data/mappings/ai-infrastructure.json (status COMPLETE, audit PASS, fingerprint current) to one ACTIVE, role-evidenced placement, one official mapped listing, and one COMPLETE O2 profile under data/companies/. 6 rows across 4 of the chain's 12 links: power-equipment 3 (ETN, GEV, POWL), liquid-cooling 1 (VRT), grid-interconnect 1 (MYRG), energy-generation 1 (CEG). THE MONEY CORNER IS COVERED: power-equipment is this chain's only money-corner link and it carries the most rows here, three of six, all with verbatim-verified earnings quotes. A name is listed ONCE, under the link that surfaced it (method section 6); its other ACTIVE placements are recorded on the row in secondary_links rather than as duplicate rows, so ETN also sits on liquid-cooling, VRT also on the money-corner power-equipment link, and GEV on energy-generation and grid-interconnect as well. VRT is deliberately kept on liquid-cooling rather than promoted to the money corner, because that is the link the existing FINAL dive data/stocks/VRT__ai-infrastructure.json is attributed to and moving it would orphan that attribution. WHAT IS NOT HERE, named rather than left silent: eight links produced no row (networking-optics, foundry, advanced-packaging, hbm-memory, ai-accelerators, hyperscale-datacenters, frontier-models, ai-applications). This is a PROFILE gap, not a census gap and not a finding about those links: the mapping places 10 issuers on each of them, but a campaign-v1 row requires a COMPLETE O2 profile and only six exist in the whole repo. foundry and advanced-packaging are CHOKE_POINT links and outrank three of the four worked links on priority; they are unworked purely because their issuers are unprofiled and mostly non-SEC (2330.TW, 005930.KS, 000660.KS, 600584.SS, 002156.SZ, 6239.TW). TWO NAMES WERE MOVED OUT, NOT DELETED: HPS-A.TO (Hammond Power Solutions) and ENR.DE (Siemens Energy) are preserved whole in superseded_rows with their reasons; both are mapped with ACTIVE placements and neither has a profile yet, and ENR.DE additionally carried another company's CIK. Every number on every row is read from data/market/<T>.json or computed from it and names its field; every quote is verified verbatim against data/edgar/docs/<T>.json by tools/check_screen.py.

data_gaps: Eight of twelve links produced no row: networking-optics, foundry, advanced-packaging, hbm-memory, ai-accelerators, hyperscale-datacenters, frontier-models, ai-applications. The mapping places ten issuers on each; none of those issuers has a COMPLETE profile, which a campaign-v1 row requires. Unblocked by run profile --campaign CAMP-20260830-01, not by more screening.

HAMMOND-POWER-SOLUTIONS (listing TSX-HPS.A, ticker HPS.A) is moved to superseded_rows: no COMPLETE profile, and the legacy row carried the vendor symbol HPS-A.TO rather than the mapped listing ticker. ACTIVE money-corner placement; a live candidate, not a rejection.

SIEMENS-ENERGY (listing XETRA-ENR, ticker ENR) is moved to superseded_rows: no COMPLETE profile, and its recorded cik 1632790 belonged to a different, US, filer. Siemens Energy AG is not an SEC filer on this plane and has no CIK here, so no verbatim quote is reachable and fundamentals must come from the annual report via web with INFERRED tags per method section 6. That work is not done.

GEV has no balance sheet in companyfacts: Piotroski (long_term_debt_fy), Beneish (ppe_net_fy, long_term_debt_fy) and the reverse DCF (enterprise_value) are all PENDING_DATA, so GEV alone carries no market-implied growth column and cannot support a dive gap table.

Piotroski is PENDING_DATA on four of six rows (ETN, GEV, POWL, CEG) and Beneish on three (ETN, GEV, CEG). Each row names the exact missing companyfacts field in quality_basis. These are input-coverage gaps in data/market/, not earnings-quality findings.

theme_revenue_exposure is null on all six rows: not one of these filers discloses a data-center-attributable revenue percentage in the document on disk. Undisclosed, never estimated (method section 6).

PCS Axis A is a retail-attention measure and reads DARK on five of six rows while Axis B reads SATURATED on all six (analyst_count 4 to 33, institutional holding 82% to 104%). The two axes disagree and Axis A is advisory; nothing here rests on it. MYRG's held_pct_institutions of 1.03798 exceeds 100%, which is a vendor artifact and is reported as fetched rather than clipped.

taste_filtered.rule: TASTE-001 rare-earth miners and TASTE-002 Taiwan concentration were applied to all eight names considered (the six admitted plus the two superseded); neither matched. TASTE-002 would filter foundry-link and advanced-packaging-link names once those links become screenable, which is one more reason the unworked links are named explicitly in universe_note.

notes.text: PCS crowdedness is reported on every row and is load-bearing for nothing. This run is the clearest evidence yet that it should not be: Axis A reads ETN, a widely-held electrical major, as DARK at 100.0 on three retail-attention fields with media null. Axis A measures RETAIL chatter, so a DARK read on a large cap is a coverage artifact, not an attention gap. method section 3 already prints PCS as ADVISORY; this row-set is why that matters.

The eight unworked links are not a judgment about those links. Six COMPLETE profiles exist in the entire repository and all six sit on four links, so link coverage here is exactly a mirror of profile coverage. Reading this file as 'the chain's other eight links found nothing' would be the wrong inference; the census placed ten issuers on each of them and nobody has profiled one yet.
